frozen_factual_contract.underlying_action: Rhea Calder v. Cinder Lake Health Network, Inc., a fictional federal-question retaliation action under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(h); the writ materials make no merits conclusion on that claim.
frozen_factual_contract.privilege_governing_law: Federal common-law privilege applies under Rule 501 because the frozen underlying action is federal-question litigation.
frozen_factual_contract.waiver_trigger: Cinder Lake's August 21, 2025 pre-suit compliance response to a federal health-program oversight office states that outside counsel reviewed Calder's federal-program billing reports and that Cinder Lake adopted identified remedial measures, but it neither quotes nor summarizes counsel's communications, witness communications, mental impressions, or legal analysis. The same nonprivileged letter is later placed in the district record as public L07; the alleged Rule 502(a) predicate remains the August 21 disclosure to a federal office.
frozen_factual_contract.rule502d_boundary: The January 9, 2026 Rule 502(d) order governs later litigation disclosures. It neither retroactively erases nor creates any waiver from the pre-suit August 21 letter.
frozen_factual_contract.lower_sealed_filing_contract: The chronology preserves January 29 for the L08/L09 memorandum exchange and February 5 for the L10/L11 log exchange outside CM/ECF; neither exchange is an electronic court filing. All four documents use February 26 as filed_on because L13 and L14 then supply the public Local Civil Rule 79.2 motion, public notice/certificate, outside-CM/ECF service proof, offline-copy provenance, and provisional lodgment of the proposed sealed exhibits; L23 later records those public docket events.
frozen_factual_contract.district_ruling: The March 25 order equates the shared topic and announced remediation with disclosure of privileged advice, finds categorical subject-matter waiver, and orders the complete investigation files produced by April 1, seven calendar days later.
frozen_factual_contract.actual_disposition: Grant the writ in part; vacate the categorical-waiver and seven-day-production provisions; deny a blanket bar on related discovery; and remand for document-specific privilege, work-product, and discovery review.
frozen_factual_contract.deficiency_contract: The shared writ-petition route remains unbound. B01 omits essential materials, respondent service, and the trial-judge-copy certification. Exact B02 creates a case-specific two-calendar-day cure deadline, and exact B03 cures the identified defects before the deadline. The future trace ends live in submitted status.
frozen_factual_contract.accepted_branch_contract: A01 and B04 are conforming accepted petition instances. B04 includes the public August 21 letter, challenged March 25 order, and preservation orders required for technical acceptance, but is substantively insufficient because it omits the public memorandum and privilege-log counterparts and item-level comparative evidence needed to establish a clear and indisputable right. It is not a technical-deficiency reason branch. Full downstream filing-instance predicates distinguish A01, B03, and B04.
frozen_factual_contract.answer_contract: An answer is not due merely because a petition was accepted. Only exact A12 invites and schedules an answer, and only then may exact A13 be accepted.
frozen_factual_contract.argument_contract: Local Rule 21 ordinarily omits oral argument. Only exact A15 expressly orders expedited argument for April 21, and the argument-held operation requires that order, a matching schedule, and the reached date.
frozen_factual_contract.emergency_contract: Emergency relief is serialized before answer and merits operations. The pack makes no claim that the engine models parallel stay and merits tracks.
frozen_factual_contract.post_disposition_boundary: Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 21(b)(7) requires the clerk to send a copy of the final disposition to the trial-court judge. In the authored fictional record, the clerk transmits that copy on the judgment date. Rule 40 applies to original proceedings as other proceedings, while Fourth Circuit guidance states that no mandate issues in an original proceeding. Each terminal future workflow therefore closes by advancing the exact fourteen-day Rule 40 deadline after disposition, with no mandate or IssueMandate operation.
frozen_factual_contract.reasoning_boundary: The workflow uses exact document and filing-instance predicates and does not infer legal sufficiency, privilege, waiver, or reason-sensitive deficiency logic from filing prose.

future_trace_contract.outcome: serialized emergency stay, exact answer order, answer, reply, express argument order, argument, partial grant, judgment, same-day clerk transmittal, and termination after the exact fourteen-day Rule 40 deadline reaches; no mandate or IssueMandate operation
deficiency, exact timely cure, and live submitted endpoint

conforming acceptance, substantive summary denial without answer or argument, judgment, same-day clerk transmittal, and termination after the exact fourteen-day Rule 40 deadline reaches; no mandate or IssueMandate operation

frozen_factual_contract.source_authority_date_boundary: Every fictional source document may cite only authority issued or effective by its own date. Later official compilations may verify unchanged preexisting statutory or rule text but do not license a fictional document to cite a later-issued authority. District sources before March 23, 2026 do not cite the March 23 Fourth Circuit rulebook. Appellate sources may cite that rulebook. In re Fluor is always labeled unpublished and nonprecedential and is used only for its exact persuasive seven-day production and no-disclosed-communication analogy.

media_boundary.reason: The successor corpus is PDF-only. District sealed materials are modeled from provenance-verified offline paper copies available to an entitled fictional party; no workbench state represents PACER or CM/ECF access to a sealed or restricted document.

projection_counts.single_disclosure_grant_anchor_rule: 350 plus the selected disclosure's page count

sealed_record_twins.mapping_rule: Each page in every equal-page pair receives one record-unique stable logical anchor mapped to one public-redacted physical anchor and one sealed physical anchor. Case, issue, disposition, and question resources reference stable logical anchors for paired content.
sealed_record_twins.remaining_stable_anchor_id_template: For each disclosure page offset not listed above, use ca4m4.cinder.anchor.stable.<disclosure-suffix>.page-<two-digit-one-based-offset>; listed semantic IDs replace the template ID at their exact offsets.
sealed_record_twins.verification_rule: A workbench session grant is per disclosure and exact resolved pack closure. Revocation removes the sealed row and restores the public projection. Every authorized open independently verifies CAS path, size, digest, PDF readability, and page count before exposing a leased snapshot. For district material, the verified source is an entitled fictional party's offline paper copy obtained and served outside CM/ECF under Standing Order 25-SO-1; the grant never represents electronic court access.
